draft.title: Second-person and third-person narration
card: The narrator speaks to the reader as you, as if the reader is the character. It can feel direct and close, and it is less common than the other types.
The narrator is outside the story and uses he, she or they to tell it. The narrator is not a character who says I.
A third-person narrator who is limited stays with one character. The reader learns only what that character sees, thinks and feels.
A third-person narrator who is omniscient knows everything. It can reveal the thoughts of many characters and events happening in other places.
draft.remember: You means second person. He, she or they means third person, either limited to one character or omniscient.

a.q: Which sentence is written in the second person?
opts: You push open the gate and hear the dog bark
I push open the gate and hear the dog bark
She pushes open the gate and hears the dog bark
They push open the gate and hear the dog bark
a.why: Second person speaks to the reader as you, so the reader becomes the character. The sentence with I is first person, and the sentences with she and they are third person.
a.clue: Look for the word that talks straight to the reader.

b.q: A story follows Leila on her first day at a new school in Orange. The narrator says she feels sick with nerves. It also says the teacher is secretly worried about her class, and that the principal is thinking about lunch. Which narration is this?
b.why: The narrator uses she and knows the private thoughts of Leila, the teacher and the principal. A narrator who knows what many characters think is omniscient. A limited narrator would stay with Leila only.
b.clue: Count how many characters' thoughts the narrator reveals.

a.best: You push open the gate and hear the dog bark
